description: This Dart source file defines the ApiClient class, which provides methods for making HTTP requests (GET, POST, DELETE, multipart POST) to a backend API, with built-in handling for authorization, error parsing, and token refresh logic. It serves as a client wrapper over the http package for Flutter applications.

classes.name: ApiClient
classes.description: A client class for interacting with a REST API, handling authentication, request building, error handling, and token refresh logic.

methods.name: ApiClient
methods.description: Constructor that initializes the API client with session and auth service dependencies, and sets the base URL from environment variables.

methods.name: _uri
methods.description: Creates a Uri object combining the base URL with a relative path and optional query parameters.

methods.name: _headers
methods.description: Builds the HTTP headers, including content type, accept, and authorization token if available.

methods.name: _handle
methods.description: Handles HTTP responses, parsing successful responses, managing 401 unauthorized errors with token refresh, and throwing appropriate ApiError exceptions.

methods.name: get
methods.description: Performs an HTTP GET request, parses the response, and retries once if a token refresh occurs.

methods.name: post
methods.description: Performs an HTTP POST request with optional body, headers, and retries once upon token refresh.

methods.name: delete
methods.description: Performs an HTTP DELETE request with retry logic for token refresh.

methods.name: multipartPost
methods.description: Simulates a multipart POST request with fields and files, currently using JSON encoding for development purposes.
